extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (mathematicians and developers) computing modular forms and modular symbols
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/specification for PARI/GP library functions handling modular forms and modular symbols: their inputs, outputs, flags, error conditions, performance notes, and example usage. Intended to guide correct use and interpretation of each function's return values.

rubrics_metrics.name: mfsymboleval path-limit definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: mfsymboleval(ES,[a,oo]) is the limit as T → ∞ of integral expressions involving (X − τ)^{k−2} F(τ) plus a(0)(X − iT)^{k−1}/(k − 1), where a(0) is the 0th coefficient of F at infinity; similarly mfsymboleval(ES,[0,a]) is the corresponding limit with b(0)(1 + iT X)^{k−1}/(k − 1) where b(0) is the 0th coefficient of F|kS at infinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the limiting definitions used when evaluating modular symbol paths that end at infinity; library syntax: GEN mfsymboleval(GEN fs, GEN path, GEN ga = NULL, long bit-prec). Examples show computed series and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: mftaylor: canonical Taylor expansion at tau = i
rubrics_metrics.description: mftaylor(F, n, {flreal = 0}). Given F in Mk(SL2(Z)), computes the first n+1 canonical Taylor expansion coefficients of F around τ = I. If flreal=0, computes only an algebraic equivalence class; if flreal is set, compute pn such that for τ close enough to I we have f(τ) = (2I/(τ+I))^k sum_{n>=0} pn((τ−I)/(τ+I))^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mftaylor(GEN F, long n, long flreal, long prec). Example: mftaylor(Delta,8) returns list of coefficients. flreal controls whether to compute a representative valid for τ near I.

rubrics_metrics.name: mftobasis: coefficients of a form on a chosen basis
rubrics_metrics.description: mftobasis(mf, F, {flag = 0}). Return coefficients of the form F on the basis given by mfbasis(mf). A q-expansion or vector of coefficients can be given instead of F but may produce an error if expansion is too short or if F does not belong to the modular form space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag is set, instead of error messages the output is an affine space of solutions if a q-expansion/vector is given, or the empty column otherwise. If F doesn't belong to the space, the result may be incorrect (matches coefficients up to some bound) and may return empty column or error. When flag=1 and insufficient data, returns [v, K] where v is a solution and K a matrix describing affine space of potential solutions. Library syntax: GEN mftobasis(GEN mf, GEN F, long flag). Examples illustrate correct, ambiguous, and incorrect cases and the resulting errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: mftocoset: find coset representative
rubrics_metrics.description: mftocoset(N, M, Lcosets). Given M in SL2(Z) and Lcosets = mfcosets(N) a list of right cosets of Γ0(N), find the coset to which M belongs. Output is pair [γ, i] such that M = γ Lcosets[i], γ ∈ Γ0(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mftocoset(long N, GEN M, GEN Lcosets). Example provided demonstrating output.

rubrics_metrics.name: mftonew: decompose cusp form into newforms data
rubrics_metrics.description: mftonew(mf, F). For mf a full or cuspidal space [N,k,χ] and F a cusp form in that space, returns a vector of 3-component vectors [M, d, G] where f(χ)|M|N, d|N/M, and G is a form in S_new(Γ0(M), χ) such that F equals the sum of B(d)(G) over all such triples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mftonew(GEN mf, GEN F). Example shows extracting [M,d,G] and matching coefficients of F and G. Useful to find newform constituents and their multiplicative shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: mftraceform: trace form in subspace of Sk(Γ0(N),χ)
rubrics_metrics.description: mftraceform(NK, {space = 0}). If NK = [N, k, CHI, .] with k integral, gives the trace form in the corresponding subspace of Sk(Γ0(N), χ). Supported space values: 0=newspace (default), 1=full cuspidal space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mftraceform(GEN NK, long space). Examples show returned q-coefficients for given NK.

rubrics_metrics.name: mftwist: twist a generalized modular form by integer D
rubrics_metrics.description: mftwist(F, D). Given a generalized modular form F, returns the twist G such that mfcoef(G,n) = (D/n) mfcoef(F,n) where (D/n) is the Kronecker symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: twisting multiplies the level by D^2 and is not an involution. Library syntax: GEN mftwist(GEN F, GEN D). Examples demonstrate twisting, effect on coefficients and params; shows composition not necessarily identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: msatkinlehner: Atkin-Lehner involution matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: msatkinlehner(M, Q, {H}). Let M be full modular symbol space of level N as given by msinit, Q | N with (Q, N/Q)=1, and H a subspace stable under Atkin-Lehner w_Q. Return the matrix of w_Q acting on H (or M if H omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN msatkinlehner(GEN M, long Q, GEN H = NULL). Examples: compute involution matrix w and verify w^2 == 1; #w gives dimension. Works on +/− parts when M initialized with sign parameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: mscuspidal: cuspidal part and optional decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: mscuspidal(M, {flag = 0}). For M a full modular symbol space, return its cuspidal part S. If flag=1, return [S, E], its decomposition into cuspidal and Eisenstein parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subspace is represented by a structure whose first component is matrix with integer coefficients whose columns form a Q-basis. Library syntax: GEN mscuspidal(GEN M, long flag). Examples show returned matrices for S and E and how they correspond to dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: msdim: dimension of modular symbol space
rubrics_metrics.description: msdim(M). For M a full modular symbol space or subspace (as from msinit or mscuspidal), return its dimension as a Q-vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: mfdim([N,k]) is faster if only dimension is needed and not full space. Library syntax: long msdim(GEN M). Examples show dimensions for various M.

rubrics_metrics.name: mseisenstein: return Eisenstein subspace
rubrics_metrics.description: mseisenstein(M). For M a full modular symbol space, return its Eisenstein subspace. The subspace is given by a structure whose first component is a matrix with integer coefficients whose columns form a Q-basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This basis matches the second component of mscuspidal(M,1). Library syntax: GEN mseisenstein(GEN M). Examples show equality check with mscuspidal(...)[2].

rubrics_metrics.name: mseval: evaluate modular symbol on a path
rubrics_metrics.description: mseval(M, s, {p}). Given M a full modular symbol space, s a modular symbol element of M, and p = [a,b] ∈ ∆ a path between two cusps, return s(p) ∈ V. Paths can be given as integers, fractions, oo, or as 2x2 integer matrices whose columns give cusps. s can be t_COL (modular symbol in chosen basis), t_MAT (matrix of symbols), or t_VEC (values on path generators). If p omitted, convert s to vector of s(gi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the returned values are de-homogenized corresponding to y = 1. For t_MAT input, faster evaluation for many symbols on same path. Library syntax: GEN mseval(GEN M, GEN s, GEN p = NULL). Examples show returned polynomials and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: msfromcusp: modular symbol attached to a cusp
rubrics_metrics.description: msfromcusp(M, c). Returns the modular symbol attached to cusp c where M is modular symbol space of level N. Cusp c in P1(Q)/G is given as oo or rational a/b. The symbol maps path [b]-[a] to Ec(b)-Ec(a) where Ec(r)=0 when r==c and X^{k-2}|γ_r otherwise, these symbols span the Eisenstein subspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If M initialized with non-zero sign, the returned symbol is given in terms of fixed basis of whole symbol space, not necessarily the ± part. Library syntax: GEN msfromcusp(GEN M, GEN c). Examples show returned vectors and evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: msfromell: modular symbol(s) attached to an elliptic curve
rubrics_metrics.description: msfromell(E, {sign = 0}). For E/Q elliptic curve of conductor N, returns [M,x] where M = msinit(N,2) and x is x_sign for sign=±1, or x=[x+, x−, LE] when sign=0; x± are modular symbols normalized by periods Ω± and satisfy Hecke eigenrelations Tp(xε)=ap xε for p∤N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on normalization: F = x+Ω+ + x− iΩ−; relations link values at cusps to L-values L(E,1)/Ω+. Returns modular symbols as t_COL. Library syntax: GEN msfromell(GEN E, long sign). Examples show returned vectors, Hecke checks, and handling of vector of isogenous curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: msfromhecke: basis of symbols killed by specified polynomials in Hecke operators
rubrics_metrics.description: msfromhecke(M, v, {H}). Given M and vector v of pairs [p,P] (p prime and P polynomial with integer coefficients), return a basis of modular symbols s such that P(Tp)(s)=0. If H present restrict to H. If P(x)=x-ap degree 1, ap integer accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN msfromhecke(GEN M, GEN v, GEN H = NULL). Examples show constructing subspace from eigenvalues or characteristic polynomials and verifying Hecke action and characteristic polynomial factoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: msgetlevel: return level N of modular symbol space
rubrics_metrics.description: msgetlevel(M). For M a full modular symbol space as given by msinit, return its level N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long msgetlevel(GEN M). Simple getter function.

rubrics_metrics.name: msgetsign: return sign parameter of modular symbol space
rubrics_metrics.description: msgetsign(M). For M a full modular symbol space as given by msinit, return its sign: ±1 or 0 (unset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long msgetsign(GEN M). Example demonstrates sign returned for msinit(...,1) vs default.

rubrics_metrics.name: msgetweight: return weight k of modular symbol space
rubrics_metrics.description: msgetweight(M). For M a full modular symbol space as given by msinit, return its weight k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long msgetweight(GEN M). Example shows msgetweight(msinit(11,4)) => 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: mshecke: Hecke operator matrices on modular symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: mshecke(M, p, {H}). For M a full modular symbol space, p a prime, and H a Hecke-stable subspace (M if omitted), return the matrix of Tp acting on H (Up if p divides N). Result undefined if H not stable by Tp (resp. Up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mshecke(GEN M, long p, GEN H = NULL). Examples show T2 matrices for various signed spaces, action on new subspace and comparison to ellap values. Use msnew(M)[1] to restrict to newspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: msinit: initialize modular symbol space
rubrics_metrics.description: msinit(G, V, {sign = 0}). Given G finite index subgroup of SL2(Z) and representation V of GL(2,Q), create space M = Hom_G(Div0(P1(Q)), V). If sign present and non-zero it must be ±1 and we consider Ker(σ - sign). Currently supported groups: Γ0(N) coded by integer N>0. Supported representation: Vk = Q[X,Y]^{k-2} coded by integer k≥2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN msinit(GEN G, GEN V, long sign). Returned M encodes Z[G]-generators and canonical Q-basis used by other functions. Examples show msinit usage, msdim, mshecke, msstar, and +/− parts via sign parameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: msissymbol: check if vector/matrix is modular symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: msissymbol(M, s). For M a full modular symbol space, check whether s is a modular symbol attached to M; if A is a matrix, check whether its columns represent modular symbols and return a 0-1 vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN msissymbol(GEN M, GEN s). The function checks relations among generator values; will return 0 if relations violated. Examples show msissymbol returning 1 for valid symbol, 0 for perturbed symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: mslattice: canonical Z-structure on a subspace H
rubrics_metrics.description: mslattice(M, {H}). For M a modular symbol space and H a subspace (defaults to cuspidal part), return a canonical Z-basis of the inverse image by c : M→H^1(Γ0(N), Vk) of H^1(Γ0(N), Lk) in the space of modular symbols generated by H. Eisenstein part is in kernel of c so result has no meaning for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H can be given by a matrix representing its Q-basis. Library syntax: GEN mslattice(GEN M, GEN H = NULL). Examples show returned Z-bases for S and E and note degeneracy for Eisenstein part.

rubrics_metrics.name: msnew: return new part of cuspidal subspace
rubrics_metrics.description: msnew(M). For M a full modular symbol space, return the new part of its cuspidal subspace. Subspace represented by structure whose first component is matrix with integer coefficients and columns forming Q-basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN msnew(GEN M). Example shows msnew(M) and dimension of returned newspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: msomseval: moments of p-adic distribution attached to path
rubrics_metrics.description: msomseval(Mp, PHI, path). Return vectors of moments of the p-adic distribution attached to the path by the overconvergent modular symbol PHI (Mp from mspadicinit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN msomseval(GEN Mp, GEN PHI, GEN path). Example shows use after mspadicinit and mstooms to produce ME = msomseval(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: mspadicL: p-adic L-function values/derivatives from moments
rubrics_metrics.description: mspadicL(mu, {s = 0}, {r = 0}). Returns the value (or r-th derivative) on a character χ_s of Z_p^* of the p-adic L-function attached to mu, where mu is as returned by mspadicmoments. s encodes p-adic character parameters; r is derivative order. When ap is p-adic unit values in Q_p, otherwise in 2-dim Q_p-vector space D_cris(M(φ)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mu must be distributions attached to an overconvergent symbol PHI. Library syntax: GEN mspadicL(GEN mu, GEN s = NULL, long r). Examples show computing L_p at various characters, derivatives, and effects of twists. Explanatory formulas included in doc for interpretation of s and mu.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspadicinit: initialize data for overconvergent modular symbols modulo p^n
rubrics_metrics.description: mspadicinit(M, p, n, {flag}). Given M a modular symbol space and p prime, initialize technical data to compute with overconvergent modular symbols modulo p^n. If flag unset allow all symbols; else initialize only restricted range: flag=0 restricts to ordinary symbols; higher flag restricts to symbols with v_p(ap) >= flag. For supersingular eigensymbols (p | ap) must assume p ∤ level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function uses O(N^2 (n+k)^2 p) memory where N is level of M. Restricting by flag may cause exceptions if eigenvalue valuations violate bound. Library syntax: GEN mspadicinit(GEN M, long p, long n, long flag). Examples show correct/incorrect usages and error messages when constraints violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspadicmoments: compute distributions (moments) from overconvergent eigensymbol
rubrics_metrics.description: mspadicmoments(Mp, PHI, {D = 1}). Given Mp from mspadicinit, an overconvergent eigensymbol PHI from mstooms and discriminant D coprime to p, compute the distribution µ = PHI_D([0]−[∞])|_{Z_p^*} restricted to Z_p^* and return moments of p−1 distributions on residue discs (a + p Z_p), 0<a<p. PHI may be given as classical symbol (lifted) but that is wasteful for multiple twists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned µ can be used by mspadicL or mspadicseries. Library syntax: GEN mspadicmoments(GEN Mp, GEN PHI, long D). Examples illustrate ordinary case, twisting, and subsequent mspadicL outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspadicseries: compute p-adic power series from moments
rubrics_metrics.description: mspadicseries(mu, {i = 0}). Given µ distribution from overconvergent symbol, compute ˆL_p(µ, τ^i)(x) = ∫_{Z_p^*} τ^i(t) (1+x)^{log_p(t)/log_p(u)} dµ(t). Returns p-adic series with maximal precision given µ. Parameter i picks Teichmüller power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: u is chosen multiplicative generator (1+p for p>2, 5 for p=2). Library syntax: GEN mspadicseries(GEN mu, long i). Examples show series output, behavior for supersingular examples with negative p-adic valuations, and relation to mspadicL. Notes on precision and examples with twists included.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspathgens: return Z[G]-generators and relations for Div0(P1(Q))
rubrics_metrics.description: mspathgens(M). For M a full modular symbol space, return [g,R] where g is minimal system of generators (paths) and R vector of Z[G]-relations between them. Relations are coded as vectors of pairs [a_i, i] with a_i ∈ Z[G] and i index of generator, so that sum_i a_i g[i] = 0. Paths coded as [u,v] with oo for infinity. Z[G] elements can be integers or factorization matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output depends only on group G, not on representation V. Library syntax: GEN mspathgens(GEN M). Examples show returned generators, number and form of relations, and how relations correspond to torsion elements or round trips among cusps.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspathlog: express a path in Z[G]-generator coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: mspathlog(M, p). Given M with fixed Z[G]-generators (from mspathgens) and a path p = [a,b], return (p_i) in Z[G] such that p = sum_i p_i g_i. Path extremities can be integers, fractions, oo, or given by 2x2 integer matrix columns. Output depends only on group G not representation V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mspathlog(GEN M, GEN p). Examples show returned factorization matrices for path and equivalence check when giving path as 2x2 matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspetersson: intersection product / Petersson pairing via modular symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: mspetersson(M, {F}, {G = F}). For M a full modular symbol space for Γ0(N), compute intersection product {F,G} of modular symbols F and G on M = Hom_Γ(∆, Vk) extended to Hermitian bilinear form on M ⊗ C whose radical is Eisenstein subspace. If F omitted, treat as full modular space attached to M; if G omitted, take equal to F. Allows F and G matrices and returns Gram matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains relation to Petersson inner product: {F^R_1,F^R_2} = −2(2i)^{k−2} <f1,f2>_Petersson and {F1,¯F2} = (2i)^{k−2} <f1,f2>_Petersson. In weight 2, {F,G} integer-valued on mslattice Z-structure and relates to modular degree. Library syntax: GEN mspetersson(GEN M, GEN F = NULL, GEN G = NULL). Examples show Gram matrices, link to elliptic curve modular degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspolygon: construct Farey symbol / hyperbolic polygon for Γ0(N)
rubrics_metrics.description: mspolygon(M, {flag = 0}). Given N>1 return hyperbolic polygon (Farey symbol) attached to Γ0(N): vertices a list in P1(Q) representing cusps; edges hyperbolic arcs joining consecutive vertices; involution e→e* and pairing matrices G giving γ_e ∈ Γ0(N) with e = γ_e e*. Returned data: list E of edges (matrices), permutation A, list G of pairing matrices. Binary digits of flag: 1 return normalized polygon (distance conditions) else unimodular edges; 2 add LaTeX graphical representations. Normalized polygon properties described (distance constraints, cusps, elliptic points, genus info).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mspolygon(GEN M, long flag). Examples include normalized vs non-normalized, extraction of A permutation vector, determinants of edge matrices, how polygon structure reflects genus, cusps, elliptic points, and system of generators for Γ0(N). Graphics output can be included in LaTeX via tikz strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: msqexpansion: compute Fourier coefficients of normalized newform
rubrics_metrics.description: msqexpansion(M, projH, {B = seriesprecision}). Given M and projH projector on Hecke-simple subspace (from mssplit), return Fourier coefficients a_n, n ≤ B, of corresponding normalized newform. If B omitted use seriesprecision. msqexpansion(M, s, B) shortcut accepts Hecke eigenvector s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm naive O(B^2 d^3) where d = O(kN) is dimension of Mk(Γ0(N)). Library syntax: GEN msqexpansion(GEN M, GEN projH, long precdl) or shortcut with symbol. Examples show equality with elliptic curve an sequence computed by ellan.

rubrics_metrics.name: mssplit: split Hecke-stable subspace into Hecke-simple pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: mssplit(M, {H}, {dimlim}). For M = msinit(N,k,±1) and H a Hecke-stable subspace of msnew(M) (or full new subspace if H omitted), split H into Hecke-simple subspaces. If dimlim present and positive, restrict to subspaces of dimension ≤ dimlim. Subspace represented by structure whose first component is matrix with integer coefficients whose columns form Q-basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mssplit(GEN M, GEN H = NULL, long dimlim). Used to obtain irreducible Hecke orbits; examples in surrounding text show combining with msnew, msqexpansion, mspadic computations.
